news.title: QQQ vs. VGT: Where Should You Invest $1,000 Right Now?
news.description: The article compares two tech-focused ETFs: Invesco QQQ (tracking Nasdaq-100) and Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT). QQQ offers better diversification with ~30% non-tech holdings providing downside protection, while VGT is a pure tech play with lower expenses (0.09% vs 0.10%). The author recommends QQQ for its balance amid inflation concerns and geopolitical risks, though both ETFs remain viable for those bullish on AI-driven earnings growth.

vendor_sentiment.reasoning: Recommended as the better choice due to sector diversification (30% non-tech), exposure to semiconductor leaders (Micron, Lam Research, Applied Materials), and downside protection against tech-focused market tumbles amid inflation and geopolitical concerns.

news.title: What History Says About Stocks That Join the Nasdaq-100 and What It Means for SpaceX
news.description: SpaceX was added to the Nasdaq-100 on July 7, 2026, and initially dropped 17% in its first 10 days, following historical patterns where most new index additions decline in their first week. However, historical data shows stocks added to the Nasdaq-100 typically gain 3.6% after one month and 6.3% after three months. SpaceX's long-term prospects depend on capturing its $26.5 trillion addressable market in AI infrastructure, with potential revenue from computing capacity deals with Alphabet, Anthropic, and the Department of Defense, though the company faces significant capital expenditure requirements and already substantial losses.

vendor_sentiment.reasoning: The ETF is mentioned as a tracker of the Nasdaq-100 that was required to purchase SpaceX shares upon its inclusion. SpaceX now comprises 1.1% of the portfolio. This is a factual relationship with no inherent positive or negative implication for the ETF itself.
